Disclosure  to  Promote  the  Right  To  Information 

Whereas  the  Parliament  of  India  has  set  out  to  provide  a  practical  regime  of  right  to 
information  for  citizens  to  secure  access  to  information  under  the  control  of  public  authorities, 
in  order  to  promote  transparency  and  accountability  in  the  working  of  every  public  authority, 
and  whereas  the  attached  publication  of  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  is  of  particular  interest 
to  the  public,  particularly  disadvantaged  communities  and  those  engaged  in  the  pursuit  of 
education  and  knowledge,  the  attached  public  safety  standard  is  made  available  to  promote  the 
timely  dissemination  of  this  information  in  an  accurate  manner  to  the  public.

Indian  Standard 

SPECIFICATION  FOR 
REELS  AND  DRUMS  FOR  BARE  CONDUCTORS 

( First  Revision ) 

0.    FOREWORD 

0*1  This  Indian  Standard  ( First  Revision )  was  adopted  by  the  Indian 
Standards  Institution  on  24  October  I960,  after  the  draft  finalized  by  the 
Conductors  and  Accessories  for  Overhead  Lines  Sectional  Committee  had 
been  approved  by  the  Electrotechnical  Division  Council. 
0.2  Indian  Standard  'Specification  for  reels  and  "drums  for  bare  wire' 
( IS  :  1776  )  was  originally  published  in  1961  while  IS :  2889  'Specification 
for  drums  for  trolley  and  contact  wire '  was  published  in  lw>4.  As  the 
requirements  for  drums  for  conductors  and  trolley  and  contact  wires  are 
essentially  the  same,  it  was  decided  while  preparing  this  standard,  to  .cover 
the  drums  for  these  two  applications  by  a  single  standard.  This-  standard, 
therefore,  supersedes  IS :  2889-1964 . 

0*3  In  this  revised  standard  the  important  dimensions  for  various  compo- 
nents of  drums,  which  were  not  covered  in  the  earlier  standard,  have  also 
been  specified. 

0.4  For  the  purpose  of  deciding  whether  a  particular  requirement  of  this 
standard  is  complied  with,  the  final  value,  observed  or  calculated*  expressing 
the  result  of  a  test,  shall  be  rounded  off  in  acordance  with  IS:  2-1960*. 
The  number  of  significant  places  retained  in  the  rounded  off  value  should 
be  the  same  as  that  of  the  specified  value  in  this  standard. 


1.  SCOPE 

1.1  This  standard  specifies  the  requirements  for  wooden   drums   for 
overhead  line  conductors. 

1*2  This  standard  also  covers  the  requirements  for  drums  for  trolley  and 
contact  wires. 

2.  NOMENCLATURE 

2*1  For  the  purpose  of  this  standard,  the  names  of  the  various  component 
parts  of  drums  as  shown  in  Fig.  1  and  2  shall  apply. 

•Rules  far  rounding  off  numerical  values. 
3 


I9il77B.ll 


IBs  1978. 19tt 


IS  1 1778-1980 

3.  MATERIAL  AND  CONSTRUCTION 

3.0  The  drums  shall  be  so  constructed  and  made  from  such  materials  that 
they  satisfy  the  conditions  specified  in  this  standard.  The  flanges  and 
barrel  shall  be  free  from  protruding  material  capable  of  damaging  the 
conductor  or  the  hands  of  the  operator  during  rotation  of  the  drum.  The 
general  constructional  features  of  the  drums  shall  be  as  shown  in  Fig.  1 
and  2  and  in  Table  1. 

3.1  Wooden  Components  —  All  wooden  components  shall  be  manufac- 
tured throughout  of  seasoned  wood,  preferably  softwood.  The  wood  used 
in  the  construction  shall  be  sound  and  free  from  defects  that  materially 
weaken  the  component  parts  of  the  drums.  Wood  preservative  shall  be 
used  at  the  points  where  the  barrel  and  flange  components  meet. 
If  required  by  the  purchaser,  the  preservative  treatment  shall  be  applied 
to  the  entire  drum. 

Nora  —  If  agreed  between  the  purchaser  and  the  supplier,  the  wooden  com- 
ponents may  be  manufactured  out  of  ascu-treated  wood.  Guidance  regarding  types 
of  preservatives,  their  brief  description,  methods  of  treatment  and  the  type  and 
choice  of  treatment,  may  be  obtained  from  IS  :  401-1967*. 

3.2  Flanges  —  All  flanges  shall  be  of  2-ply  construction  irrespective  of  flange 
thickness.  Each  ply  shall  be  nailed  and  clenched  together  at  approximately  90  . 
Nails  shall  be  driven  from  the  inside  face  of  the  flange,  punched  and  then 
clenched  on  the  outer  face.  Flange  boards  shall  not  be  less  than  the  nominal 
thickness  by  more  than  2  nun.  There  shall  not  be  less  than  2  nails  per  board  in 
each  circle.  The  number  of  circles  of  nails  shall  be  in  accordance  with  Table  2. 

'Nbra — To  accommodate  different  lengths  of  the  conductor,  OugeaUametor  of  tbe  dram  may  be 
changed  as  per  the  mutual  agreement  between  the  supplier  and  the  purchaser  provided  all  other 
requirements  of  the  standard  am  fulfilled.' 

3.2.1  Where  a  slot  is  cut  in  the  flange  to  receive  the  inner  end 
of  the  conductor,  the  entrance  shall  be  in  line  with  the  periphery  of  the 
barrel. 

&Z2  The  flanges  of  the  drum  shall  be  large  enough  to  prevent  any  possible 
contact  between  the  conductors  and  the  ground  during  handling  or  transport.  The 
projection  of  the  flanges  beyond  the  outer  most  layer  of  the  conductors  shall  be  at 
least  SO  mm  for  all  drums. 

3.3  Spindle  Hole  —  The  spindle  hole  shall  be  cut  through  the  centre  of 
the  middle  flange  board  and  either  spindle  plates  or  cast  iron  bushings 
shall  be  fitted  by  bolts  and  nuts  as  required  by  the  purchaser. 

3.4  Barrel-End  Supports  —  The  supports  shall  be  securely  fixed  to  the 
flanges  by  nailing  and.  shall  be  segmental  type  or  disc  type  as  may  be 
agreed  upon  between  the  purchaser  and  the  manufacturers. 


•Code  of  practice  for  preservation  of  timber  ( stemd  rtvisio*  ). 


3.4.1  Barrel-Middle  Support  —  In  case  of  drums  having  3-ply  construction, 
disc  type  middle  barrel  supports  of  2-ply  construction  with  a  100  mm 
diameter  hole  concentric  with  the  100-mm  diameter  holes  in  the  flanges, 
shall  be  provided  at  the  centre  of  the  barrel  end  support*  as  shown  in 
Fig.  2. 

3.5  Barrel  —  Each  batten  shall  be  of  segmental  type  and  shall  be  nailed 
to  the  barrel  end  supports  with  one  nail  at  each  side  for  50  mm  wide 
boards  and  at  least  two  nails  for  all  wider  boards.  The  battens  shall  be 
closely  butted  and  provided  with  a  smooth  and  round  external  surface  to 
the  barrel.  The  edges  of  the  battens  shall  be  chamfered. 

3.6  Stretchers  —  Stretchers  may  be  used  in  the  construction  of  drums 
and  the  middle  end  supports  when  provided  shall  be  slotted  to  receive 
them.  Alternatively,  the  spindle  plate  ( bush )  bolts  shall  extend  through 
the  traverse  length  of  the  drum. 

3.7  Iron  Work  —  Normally,  nuts  on  the  barrel  bolts  or  studs  shall  stand 
proud  of  the  flange  but,  if  especially  required  on  the  smaller  drums,  the 
nuts  may  be  countersunk.  All  iron  work  shall  be  in  accordance  with  the 
dimensions  given  in  Table  2  and  shall  be  given  a  covering  of  protective 
paints. 

3.7.1  The  ends  of  bolts  or  studs  shall  be  flush  with  the  top  of  the  nuts 
or  rivetted  over  the  nut.

3.7.2  U-nails  or  bolts  of  appropriate  sizes  shall  be  provided  on  the  side 
of  one  of  the  flanges  to  secure  the  conductor  ends. 

4.  DIMENSIONS 

4*1  The  drum  sizes  shall  always  be  denoted  by  the  flange  diameter.  The 
dimensions  shall  be  in  accordance  with  Tables  1  and  2. 

5.  PROTECTIVE  ARRANGEMENT 

5.1  Protective  Wrapping  —  The  barrel  surface  and  inner  surfaces  of 
flanges  of  the  drums  meant  for  aluminium  and  steel  cor»d  aluminium 
conductor?    iall  be  painted  with  bitumen  based  paint.  A  layer  of  water- 

Sroof  material  shall  be  provided  over  the  barrel  and  the  inner  surfaces  of 
anges.  Another  layer  of  water-proof  material  shall  be  provided  over  the 
las;  iayer  of  conductor  and  under  the  laggings. 

5.2  Protective  Lagging  —  Protective  lagging,  if  required  by  the  purcha- 
ser and  stated  in  the  enquiry  or  order  shall  be  of  the  type  as  detailed 
in  5.2.1. 

5.2.1  External  Laggings 

5.2.1.1  The  external  lagging  shall  be  closely  fitted  and  shall  be  of 
the  thicknesses  given  in  Table  2. 

5.2.1.2  Recesses  of  size  30  x  2*5  mm  shall  be  made  in  each  wooden 
batten  constituting  the  external  lagging  to  accommodate  the  binders. 

5.2.1.3  Binders  consisting  of  hoop  iron  or  galvanized  steel  wire  shall 
be  provided  over  the  external  laggings. 

5.2.2  It  is  recommended  that  the  drums  having  3-pIy  construction  may 
also  be  provided  with  circumferential  battens  of  suitable  thickness  over 
the  water-proof  wrapping  to  protect  the  conductor  from  damage  during 
transit  in  the  event  of  breakage/detachment  of  the  external  laggings. 
Circumferential  battens  shall  be  fitted  suitably  to  the  external  lagging 
preferably  press  fitted  and  nails  shall  not  be  used  for  fixing  these  battens. 

8.  LABELLING  AND  MARKING 

8.1  Labelling  —  The  drum  number  shall  be  branded  or  gauged  or 
stencilled  into  the  flange.  An  arrow  shall  be  marked  on  the  sides  of  the 
drum,  together  with  the  words  *  Roll  this  way '.  The  following  particulars 
of  the  contents  of  the  drum  shall  be  provided  on  the  outside  of  the  flange 
in  such  a  manner  that  It  cannot  be  easily  removed: 

a)  Manufacturers'  name  or  trade-mark, 

b)  Contract/specification  number, 


IB  1 1778  -  1980 

3.7.2  U-nails  or  bolts  of  appropriate  sizes  shall  be  provided  on  the  side 
of  one  of  the  flanges  to  secure  the  conductor  ends. 

4.  DIMENSIONS 

4*1  The  drum  sizes  shall  always  be  denoted  by  the  flange  diameter.  The 
dimensions  shall  be  in  accordance  with  Tables  1  and  2.

flanges  of  the  drums  meant  for  aluminium  and  steel  cor<»d^  aluminium 
conductor;  liall  be  painted  with  bitumen  based  paint.  A  layer  of  water- 
proof material  shall  be  provided  over  the  barrel  and  the  inner  surfaces  of 
flanges.  Another  layer  of  water-proof  material  shall  be  provided  over  the 
las;  layer  of  conductor  and  under  the  laggings. 

5.2  Protective  Lagging  —  Protective  lagging,  if  required  by  the  purcha- 
ser and  stated  in  the  enquiry  or  order  shall  be  of  the  type  as  detailed 
in  5.2.1. 

5.2.1  External  Laggings 

5.2.1.1  The  external  lagging  shall  be  closely  fitted  and  shall  be  of 
the  thicknesses  given  in  Table  2. 

5.2.1.2  Recesses  of  size  30  x  2*5  mm  shall  be  made  in  each  wooden 
batten  constituting  the  external  lagging  to  accommodate  the  binders. 

5.2.1.3  Binders  consisting  of  hoop  iron  or  galvanized  steel  wire  shall 
be  provided  over  the  external  laggings.

also  be  provided  with  circumferential  battens  of  suitable  thickness  over 
the  water-proof  wrapping  to  protect  the  conductor  from  damage  during 
transit  in  the  event  of  breakage/detachment  of  the  external  laggings. 
Circumferential  battens  shall  be  fitted  suitably  to  the  external  lagging 
preferably  press  fitted  and  nails  shall  not  be  used  for  fixing  these  battens.

stencilled  into  the  flange.  An  arrow  shall  be  marked  on  the  sides  of  the 
drum,  together  with  the  words  *  Roll  this  way '.  The  following  particulars 
of  the  contents  of  the  drum  shall  be  provided  on  the  outside  of  the  flange 
in  such  a  manner  that  it  cannot  be  easily  removed: 

a)  Manufacturers'  name  or  trade-mark,

6.2  BIS  Certification  Marking 

The  product  may  also  be  marked  with  Standard  Mark. 

6.2.1  The  use  of  the  Standard  Mark  is  governed  by  the  provisions  of  the 
Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  Act,  1986  and  the  Rules  and  Regulations  made 
thereunder.  The  details  of  conditions  under  which  the  licence  for  the  use  of 
Standard  Mark  may  be  granted  to  manufacturers  or  producers  may  be  obtained 
from  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards. 

7.  TESTS 

7.1  Type  Testa  —  The  following  shall  constitute  type  tests: 

a)  Visual  examination  (  7.3  ),  and 

b)  Barrel  batten  strength  (  7.4 ). 

7.2  Routine  Testa  —  The  following  shall  constitute  routine  test: 

Visual  examination  ( 7.3 ) 

7 3  Visual  Examination  —  Each  drum  shall  be  examined  visually  for 
good  workmanship. 

7.4  Barrel  Batten  Strength  —  The  barrel  batten  shall  have  strength 
twice  that  of  winding  tension.  The  winding  tension  may  be  obtained  from 
the  conductor  manufacturer.  The  load  shall  be  applied  in  the  middle  of 
the  barrel  in  a  manner  as  agreed  to  between  the  purhaser  and  the 
supplier.  The  barrel  battens  shall  not  show  signs  of  breaking  after  the 
application  of  this  load. 

7*4.1  In  case  the  drums  are  meant  for  tension  stringing  the  barrel 
batten  strength  shall  not  be  less  than  300  kg.
